### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-odata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **90** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c3cf43a657651ad1cec7ecd0108a4d8fd86a0194` — the merge of head `74cac048492c37f8be30631dbef4b0d5ab441ade` into base `7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c3cf43a657651ad1cec7ecd0108a4d8fd86a0194 && git checkout c3cf43a657651ad1cec7ecd0108a4d8fd86a0194
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af 74cac048492c37f8be30631dbef4b0d5ab441ade && git checkout -B drift-repro 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af && git merge --no-ff 74cac048492c37f8be30631dbef4b0d5ab441ade

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7de1bad5cbf752608dc6426621ace86c852b21af` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: REWORK at `646a10ecf607fbf227a09e2f36e149fa5c039130` (2026-11-20T22:08Z). One changeset clause, the ablation record, and one claim amendment

**Scope.** Two commits, 22 files against merge base `17ed9e7bfd` (+1,611 / −21). The claim is 7048435857 and the dev report is 7051244258. The card thread asked me three questions; each is answered below.

### The three questions

1. **B6: no caller input reaches a 5xx through the new refusals. Confirmed.**
   - Every new 500 path recognises the leaf by its brand alone: `isFixedReadLeaf`, then `readLeaf` in `shared-record-ids.ts`. It requires all of:
     - a frozen plain object,
     - every own key a data property,
     - exactly one symbol key, `Symbol.for('objectstack.filter.sharedRecordIds')`, non-enumerable and `true`,
     - and nothing else.

     JSON cannot produce that.
   - `parseFilterAST` reaches `refuseFixedReadLeafAtParse` only inside the `catch` after the shape door has already refused, and it re-throws the original refusal when no branded leaf is found. So an unbranded array-form `in` / `nin` keeps its exact 400. The PR pins that.
   - The analytics `where` guard (`refuseFixedReadLeafInWhere`) and the OData `refuseFixedReadLeaf` use the same brand test. A `ComposedReadableIds` scope is descended only through its own symbol brand.
   - So every new 500 is reachable only by in-process code that built a branded leaf. ✔
2. **B1 split to #35946, and `Fixes #35874`: accepted, on the step-3 precedent.**
   - The hook ships unwired and fails closed: no answer means decline, and the engine path answers. No producer exists before step 6, and #35946 is a dependency of step 6.
   - The release note has to say that the platform's own plugin is unwired. That is required item 1.
3. **The deviations.**
   - `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` is one row, mandated by the gate. I accept it, but it needs a record (required item 3).
   - The `where` guard in `filter-normalizer.ts` is inside the surface (`service-analytics/src/**`). It closes the same class of gap, is pinned on five spellings, and has a changeset bullet. Accepted.
   - The three unlogged refusals (`parseFilterAST`, the analytics `where` face, OData) are at doors that hold no logger. The engine seam logs its own refusal once, and the `refuseReadableIds` precedent applies. Accepted.
   - The objectql full suite was not re-run after the rebase. CI at this head (58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed) includes Test Core and its shards, so CI stands in for it. Accepted.

### What else I checked

- The OData `find` and `count` both refuse before any request is sent. The one ablation in the report (the `find` refusal removed: 11 `find` cases go red and return rows, `count` stays green) shows the pins discriminate on that driver. ✔
- The changeset is `patch` on five packages, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The published `rowFilter` now holds only the two shapes it held before, and never the leaf; the explainer pins assert the serialized decision carries no recipient. ✔

### Required

1. **The changeset's analytics bullet hides the shipped default.** It says the native path compiles the leaf "only when the host answers `AnalyticsServiceConfig.fixedReadLeafClassOf` with `null`", and that "a host that wires no answer keeps today's behaviour". The platform's own `AnalyticsServicePlugin` is such a host in this release. Read as written, the bullet tells an operator that native SQL now answers sharing-scoped reads. **Fix:** add one clause, for example "`AnalyticsServicePlugin` wires no answer in this release (#35946), so on every host today the native path declines a scope carrying the leaf and the engine path answers".
2. **Ablations: a record, no new head.** One leg covers one of seven changed compile surfaces. Run each mutation, and post the reds and the clean restores as a report amendment:
   - **(a) Native compile, leaf dropped.** In `compileScopedFilterToSql`, compile the leaf as no restriction. The live case-set rows on SQLite should go red: the one that returns `n3` too, and `n5`.
   - **(b) Native compile, inner read walled.** Add a tenant predicate to the subquery. The nested-under-tenant case and `g7` should go red, as they did in step 3.
   - **(c) Decline forced off.** Make `readScopeCarriesUncompilableFixedReadLeaf` answer `false`. The no-hook and `beforeFind`-hook decline pins should go red.
   - **(d) B6 removed.** Delete the `refuseFixedReadLeafAtParse` call. The branded array-form pins should go red (they answer 400), and the unbranded 400 pin should stay green.
   - **(e) `where` guard removed.** Skip `refuseFixedReadLeafInWhere` on both faces. The five-spelling pins should go red.
   - **(f) Explainer resolution skipped.** Pass the leaf through unresolved. The two `rowFilter` shape pins and the no-recipient pin should go red.
3. **A claim amendment on #35874** for the file outside the surface: `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, one row (`explain-fixed-read-leaf.test.ts`, `findOne`, pinned 1), required by `check:engine-double-contract`. It is not a governed path; it only needs to be on record, as on #34352.

### For the seat (not L1's to rule)

- **#35946** (B1, dev recommendation A). It costs an `engine.ts` ceiling raise and a spec contract row. It is the maintainer's call, and it must land before step 6.
- **The optional ADR-0155 pointer note** naming `compileScopedFilterToSql` among analytics' brand-naming callers.
- **The dormant 400** at the spec comparand door for callers that name no brand, which prints `shapePreview`. It is noted in the PR body; filing it is the seat's call.

### Before landing

- A delta L1 after item 1, and records for items 2 and 3.
- CI green on that head.
- The CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS, same head (`packages/spec/src/**`, `Clause-②: yes`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81da4605fae7b790a0ecf701d1e68f2435433b5d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-fixed-read-leaf.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts

PR #35945, card #35874 (ADR-0155 plan step 5). Read with `git show` and `git diff` only.

Head. The review was done file by file at `103f93b7ac` (22 files, +1,611 / −21 against merge base `17ed9e7bfd`). The head moved during it to `81da4605fa`, one commit on top. `git diff 103f93b7ac 81da4605fa --stat` is tests only: `explain-fixed-read-leaf.test.ts`, `fixed-read-leaf-native-compile.test.ts` and `shared-record-ids.test.ts`, +36 / −18. Every file in `Scope:` is byte-identical on the two heads. I read the delta: it splits existing pins into pins of their own and adds none for the shapes S1 and S2 name, so every judgment below holds at `81da4605fa`.

Scope decision. `hits` is `filter.zod.ts` alone. I widened to every non-test source file in the diff, for two reasons. The card declares `Clause-②: yes` for the explainer's published `rowFilter` and for the analytics merges, so those are contract faces in their own right. And the `filter.zod.ts` jsdoc describes one refusal that five other doors in this diff also make (the engine seam's public readers, the analytics scope and `where` doors, the explainer, OData), so each is the code that sentence is checked against. The remainder is the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`: the five test files, `.changeset/35874-fixed-read-leaf-census-rest.md` and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`.

Inputs read: the card body and its five comments (triage 7042520953, ruling 7047007471, claim 7048435857, dev report 7051244258, claim amendment 7051811974); the PR body, its three issue comments (L1 7051798358 among them) and its file list; ADR-0155 D-0, D1, D2, D4, D5, D6, Q2 with its census and costs, Consequences, Open items and the plan; ruling record 6942854600; the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts (check-runs, read at 2026-11-20T22:39Z):

- **At `81da4605fa`, this record's head: not yet answered.** 8 success, 10 skipped, 18 in progress, none failed. The runs started about a minute before this record was written.
- **At `103f93b7ac`: 58 success, 17 skipped, 3 cancelled, none failed.** `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates`, `· consumer gates` and `· debt ledger`, every `Lint ·` family, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test UI` (16 of 16) and `Test Core` shards 2 to 8 and 10 are green. `Test Core (1/10)` and `(9/10)` were cancelled by the push of `81da4605fa`, so they gave no verdict there; the third cancel is a superseded `Check Changeset` beside two green ones.
- **At `646a10ecf6`**, whose source files are the ones in `Scope:` unchanged: every `Test Core` shard was green.
- So no gate has failed on any head of this diff, and the full test verdict on this record's head is still owed. The delta review reads it on the head that carries the fixes.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

1. **`@objectstack/spec` `parseFilterAST`: a refusal changes envelope, the accept set does not move.** When the shape door refuses a lowered condition that carries a branded leaf, the answer is `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 instead of `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Right in direction: D4 says the refusal "is not `INVALID_FILTER`: the fault is a composition's". An unbranded copy keeps 400 (the original refusal is re-thrown when no branded leaf is found). No operator, no export and no schema key is added; `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` is untouched (D1). The new imports (`./fixed-read-leaf`, `./readable-ids`) close no runtime cycle: `readable-ids.ts` imports `filter.zod` for a type only. Incomplete as written: see S1.
2. **`@objectstack/objectql`: two function exports and one type** (`fixedReadLeafClassOfEngine`, `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`, `FixedReadLeafClass`). Right: the card's carry-forward asks for exactly this public face, both are read-only, and `engine.ts` does not grow. Neither has a consumer in this release (the analytics plugin is unwired, #35946), which L1 accepted on the step-3 precedent; I agree, because the hook fails closed.
3. **`@objectstack/service-analytics`: one optional config hook** (`AnalyticsServiceConfig.fixedReadLeafClassOf`) and optional members on `DatasetScopedStrategyContext`. Right: absent, throwing, `undefined` or a class all decline; only `null` compiles. `compileScopedFilterToSql` is the one name the package index re-exports from `read-scope-sql.ts`, and its accept set widens by exactly one shape: a read-form leaf as the `$in` comparand of `id` on the object the scope reads. Every other leaf is refused 500 before a clause compiles.
4. **Analytics merges admit the brand at a second door** (`assertReadScopeComparandsRunnable` under `admitFixedReadLeaves`). Right: Q2's ruled row, word for word. Without the option the answer is `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` / 500 as before.
5. **Analytics query `where`: a leaf in any spelling is refused 500 before either strategy.** Right, and it closes a real gap: before, a bare `{ id: leaf }` was lowered as a relation condition built from the leaf's fields, which is D5's "read as an ordinary comparand".
6. **`@objectstack/plugin-security`: `ExplainEngineDeps` (exported) gains two optional members; the sharing layer's published `rowFilter` changes content.** Right: Q2's cost line says the share arm is the judged record's id when a grant admits it and is left out otherwise, and that the leaf is never published. A host that builds the deps without the resolver gets the refusal, not a silent match. The object-level `readFilter` is composed from the row-level-security parts only (`explain-engine.ts` around line 3524), so no second path publishes the leaf.
7. **`@objectstack/driver-odata`: `find` and `count` refuse the leaf before any request.** Right: R1 behind R2 for this storage row. `findOne` goes through `find`; the driver has no other verb that takes a `where`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on five packages (`spec`, `objectql`, `service-analytics`, `plugin-security`, `driver-odata`), `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct under AGENTS.md's rule: nothing a metadata author can write changes, and a non-protocol change ships `patch`, new exports included. The five packages are exactly the five the diff moves.

Clause-②: yes — correct, and present on both the PR body and the changeset. It carries no arm, which is right: no accept set narrows (every changed input was already refused) and none widens for an author. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The changeset states the shipped default (the platform's own analytics plugin wires no class answer), which was L1's required item 1.

One sentence of the changeset is not what the code does: "`parseFilterAST` now refuses a leaf in an array-form `in` / `nin` with `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 … The new message names the leaf and its table, not the recipient." That holds for the leaf as the direct comparand only (S1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1, the open question (how the analytics plugin asks the seam): escalated, correctly.** It is decision card #35946, open and the maintainer's, and #33787 is blocked on it. Shipping the hook unwired is safe here: with no hook every scope that carries a leaf declines to the engine path, and no producer writes the leaf before step 6. I checked the one way that could fail open: the decline reads `readScopedObjects`, and `AnalyticsService` builds that list and the `getReadScope` map from the same `objects` set (`analytics-service.ts` around line 2071), so no object's scope is compiled that the decline did not read.
- **D4's admission, reconciled without an ADR edit: accepted.** D4 anchors "the analytics merges" at `assertReadScopeComparandsRunnable`. The native compiler reaches the spec door only through that same function, so the callers that name a brand to `@objectstack/spec`'s `assertListComparandShapes` are still two: the engine's door and that function. Q2 separately rules that the native compiler compiles the leaf. The optional pointer note is the seat's.
- **B6 (the array form), decided to the envelope: right decision, not carried through.** See S1.
- **Three refusals are unlogged** (`parseFilterAST`, the analytics `where` door, OData), against D4's "logged at `error` once per evaluator … wherever it occurs". Accepted as a deviation (N2).
- **Compile surface 2 goes beyond B6**: accepted, it is inside the claimed surface and is the same class of gap.
- **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the claim surface**: on record as claim amendment 7051811974. Not a governed path.
- **The dormant 400 at the spec comparand door for callers that name no brand**: out of this diff, pinned by step 2. Noted, the seat's to file.
- **PostgreSQL non-text `id` (#35906)**: the native subquery adds no cast, as step 3's `driver-sql` adds none. D-0 says a card that cannot keep the same rows on such an object stops and the case goes to the maintainer; #35906 is that case and is open. Nothing writes the leaf yet, so this head changes no rows there.
- **L1 required item 2 (the six ablations)**: the brief says the record is posted on #35874. The card held five comments when I read it, the last being 7051811974, and none is an ablation record. This review used no ablation result and its findings do not depend on one; the seat should check where that record went before landing.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5)**: no finding. The analytics native path pushes the leaf down as `id IN (SELECT …)`, one statement, no `EXISTS`, no join, every value bound, no tenant scope on the inner read (① ruled A). The explainer's read of `sys_record_share` is keyed by the ids it judges and is the shape Q2 rules for that row ("one indexed read under the fixed predicate, keyed by the record ids it judges"); it materialises no caller-wide id list. OData and the two refusal doors read nothing.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. Two findings owe a delta review; both sit in fault states no producer reaches today, and both are places where the code does not do what its own contract sentence says.

**S1 (should-fix) — `parseFilterAST` moves only the direct-comparand shapes to the envelope; a leaf as a list member or under a scalar operator still answers `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 and prints the head of the recipient.**

- The jsdoc of `refuseFixedReadLeafAtParse` says the envelope covers "the leaf as an array-form `in` / `nin` comparand or list member, the shapes the door reads as a non-list". The shape door does not refuse a list member: `assertFieldListComparands` only checks that `$in` / `$nin` hold an array with no `null` member (`filter-comparand-shape.ts`, the `nullMember` arm). So `[['id', 'in', [leaf]]]` passes the `try`, and the type door, which runs outside it, refuses the member as "a plain object" with `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 (`filter-comparand-type.ts#judgeLiteralComparand` → `comparandTypeRefusal`).
- That message carries `preview(value)`, the first 40 characters of `JSON.stringify(leaf)`: `{"object":"account","recipient":"u-secr…`. The jsdoc gives "the shape door's printed the leaf's inputs, a principal's id among them" as the reason the 400 was the wrong answer to relay. The same is still true one line below the `try`.
- The same holds for `['id', '!=', leaf]`, `['id', '>', leaf]` and the other scalar operators: the shape door passes them and the type door answers 400 with the preview.
- It reaches the first consumer. The engine's array branch calls `parseFilterAST` before `collectFixedReadLeaves` (`engine-top-level.ts` around lines 1035 to 1047), so `find('account', { where: [['id', 'in', [leaf]]] })` answers 400. The object spelling of the same misplacement, `{ id: { $in: [leaf] } }`, goes through the engine's own door, where `collectFixedReadLeaves` refuses it 500. Two spellings, two envelopes: the split the card asked this step to decide ("the array-form `in`/`nin` carrying a leaf still answers 400 from `parseFilterAST`").
- No pin covers it. The new test asserts three shapes, all with the leaf as the direct comparand.
- Fix, either way: (a) make the leaf refusal cover every refusal `parseFilterAST` raises for a condition that carries a branded leaf (the type door too), and pin the list member and one scalar operator at 500 with no recipient in the message; or (b) keep the code, correct the jsdoc and the changeset bullet to "direct comparand", and name the list-member and scalar-operator 400 as a residual beside the one the PR body already names. (a) is what D4 asks for.
- While there: the exported `parseFilterAST` jsdoc still says a shape refusal is "the `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 envelope" with no exception, and the new message says `parseFilterAST` "admits [the leaf] in no position", though an array-form `=` is lowered by reference and passed on, as the same jsdoc says two sentences later.

**S2 (should-fix) — the explainer admits a leaf by the key it sits under, not by its role, so it resolves leaves the seam and the analytics compiler refuse.**

- `explain-fixed-read-leaf.ts#resolvableLeavesOf` admits a leaf whenever it is the `$in` of a key named `id` whose leaf names the explained object, at any depth and under any parent: inside a relation condition (`{ manager: { id: { $in: leaf } } }`, a self-relation), inside a list, or inside a composed `ReadableIds` scope (it never compares the leaf with the scope's own object, and passes the explained object down).
- The module header says the opposite: "a leaf anywhere but the `$in` comparand of `id` on the explained object" is refused, "never read as an ordinary comparand". D1 limits the position to the object's own `where`.
- The other two walkers in this program read roles. The engine's `collectFixedReadLeaves` refuses `{ manager: { id: { $in: leaf } } }` (its `visitField` scans every non-`$in` operand), and the analytics `findUnservedFixedReadLeaf` in this same diff refuses it as `misplaced` and tracks the scope object through a composed scope.
- Effect: for such a filter the find the explanation describes answers 500, while the explainer substitutes `[recordId]` at the misplaced position, matches it in process and publishes a `rowFilter` and a verdict. That is D5's rule broken in a fault state ("evaluates the leaf exactly, or refuses it loudly").
- Reach: none today (no producer, and the producer places the leaf at the top level). It matters because the explainer is the one evaluator with no seam in front of it (D4), so its own walk is the only position check it has.
- Fix: walk nodes and operator maps as `findUnservedFixedReadLeaf` does (a field key's plain-object value is an operator map; only its `$in` may hold a leaf; a composed scope is judged against its own object, or refused outright here), and pin one nested-relation shape beside the `$nin` pin.

What I tried to break and could not:

- **The spec refusal's reach.** `isFixedReadLeaf` requires a frozen plain object whose only symbol key is the non-enumerable brand, so no JSON, structured clone or request reaches the 500. The walk cuts cycles on the current path and descends a composed scope through its own brand.
- **The native subquery.** Built from `fixedInnerReadOf(leaf)` alone, identifiers through `quoteIdent`, every value through `bind`, the blank-id guard on the projected column, and a compile-time check that `tenantScope` is still `'none'`.
